mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.5%) signals sustained monetary accommodation, reducing equity discount rates and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through lower cost of capital for corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.5% over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 5.0% (UNRATE > 5.0%) indicates labor market deterioration that precedes corporate earnings contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0% over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous CPI inflation above 3.0% (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) and rising policy rates (FEDFUNDS > 2.0%) signal active monetary tightening that compresses equity valuations, driving negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint condition CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS > 2.0% fails to predict negative returns in more than 60% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High industrial production growth (INDPRO > 105.0) indicates robust manufacturing activity that drives corporate earnings expansion, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO > 105.0 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained housing starts above 1200.0 (HOUST > 1200.0) reflects strong consumer demand and economic confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through elevated consumer spending.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST > 1200.0 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Residential sales exceeding 550,000 million dollars (RSAFS > 550000) signals robust housing market activity that precedes increased consumer spending and corporate profits, causing positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS > 550000 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous unemployment decline below 4.0% (UNRATE < 4.0%) and payroll growth above 140,000 (PAYEMS > 140000) indicates a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint condition UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS > 140000 fails to predict positive returns in more than 60% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 5.0%) triggers expectations of prolonged restrictive monetary policy, compressing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 5.0% over any 3-year rolling window.
